mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public and national identity authority of the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, SEPBLAC and domestic Spanish AML registers, PEP databases, FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists, and internal risk-rating frameworks. Screening is required for all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, signatories, and material commercial counterparties before notarization, at the moment of registry filing, and on a rolling quarterly basis thereafter. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, non-resident shareholders originating from high-risk jurisdictions, and where payment is structured through SWIFT letters of credit or wire transfers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central - electronic name clearance service (Certificación de Denominación Social), operated through the Spanish Ministry of Justice and the official notarial/registrar network
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be in Latin-alphabet characters, expressed in Spanish or in any language using the Latin alphabet, and must include the mandatory suffix S.L. or Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. The name must not be identical or phonetically equivalent to an existing registered Spanish company, must not be misleading as to activity, and must respect Spanish constitutional, public-order, and trademark rules.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España, Estado, Ministerio, Administración, Casa Real, Corona and similar official or institutional terms requiring prior governmental or royal authorization
Banco, Caja, Seguros, Reaseguros, Gestora, Fondo and other financial-regulation tokens requiring approval from the Bank of Spain or the Ministry of Economy
International, Mundial, Iberoamericano, Centro, Instituto and similar terms where the company cannot prove a genuine territorial or institutional basis
Telecomunicaciones and Radiodifusión where the proposed company does not yet hold a valid administrative authorization for the Spanish telecommunications sector
terms contrary to law, public order, morality, or names of natural or legal persons without express consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the requested name is rejected, the promoter may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Spanish Ministry of Justice within one month from notification. The name clearance application may itself request up to three alternative denominations ranked by order of preference; the registrar proceeds to the next available alternative if the preceding one is rejected. If all alternatives are rejected, a new application and official fee are required. The negative name certificate is valid for 90 days and any reservation must be used before expiration to open the subsequent notarial incorporation process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable only as a temporary correspondence address during pre-registration and initial incorporation steps; it is not sufficient to satisfy the substantive registered-office and commercial-presence requirements for an active telecommunications equipment manufacturer. The company will need a physical establishment for tax residence, VAT and customs registration, telecom licensing, employment, and operational inspections. A virtual address may be maintained solely as an auxiliary administrative office, never as the sole registered establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated; approximately 30-35% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 18 months of operation. The likelihood rises substantially for a company engaged in telecom equipment manufacturing, applying for EU VAT treatments, claiming customs-facilitation status, or maintaining only a virtual registered office. Agencia Tributaria, SEPBLAC, customs authorities, and telecommunication regulators may each conduct independent on-site verifications.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, LSC), Articles 20-26 (incorporation parameters and deed requirements), 58-62 (SL minimum capital regime), 209-233 (administration and governance); Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) establishing the Sociedad Limitada en Formación Sucesiva (SLFS) with EUR 1.00 capital; Ley 14/2013 on transparent incorporation procedures through CIRCE/DUE.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation) and Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid (deed registration); coordinated online via CIRCE (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (notarial deed of incorporation) executed before a Spanish Notary Public and filed for inscription in the Registro Mercantil, together with provisional NIF application (Form 036) before the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of EUR 1.00 permitted under the SLFS regime (20% of annual profits allocated to legal reserve until EUR 3,000.00 is reached); standard SL requires EUR 3,000.00 fully subscribed and paid in at incorporation through a deposit in a Spanish credit institution, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) delivered to the Notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share capital of the Company, EUR 3,000.00 represented by 3,000 participating interests of EUR 1.00 each, is fully subscribed and paid in by the founding shareholders, evidenced by the bank deposit certificate filed with this Board. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is established at [Registered Office], Madrid, Spain, within the jurisdiction of the Mercantile Registry of Madrid. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Officer Name] is appointed Sole Managing Director (Administrador Único) with full management and representation powers under the bylaws, and that the appointment be registered with the Registro Mercantil and the Agencia Tributaria.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation (Certificado de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, via CIRCE online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed company names through the CIRCE/DUE single electronic window. Pay the reservation fee. The certificate confirming the chosen denomination is valid for three months and must accompany the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Copy of passports/NIEs of founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict, file alternative names in the same application or appeal the decision before the Registro Mercantil Central within 30 days; obtain a renewed name certificate before expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Capital Deposit and Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (bank) regulated by Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account in the name of the entity 'in formation' (NIF provisional references), deposit the paid-in capital (minimum EUR 1.00 or EUR 3,000.00), and request the bank certificate of capital disbursement for submission to the Notary.
required_dossiers: NIE/passport copies of shareholders and directors
Company name certificate (if requested by bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC documentation, provide enhanced beneficial ownership evidence and source-of-funds declarations; request the certificate in the Notary's approved wording if the bank issues a non-conforming format.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) in the district of the registered office, Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the Notary with all founding shareholders (or their legal representatives) and execute the public deed, incorporating the bylaws, the subscribed and paid-in capital, and the appointment of the administrator. The Notary books the deed and issues first and green copies for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Bank capital deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso)
Passports/NIEs of all shareholders and administrators
Tax forms 036/037 with provisional tax data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary refuses or observes defects, correct the capital evidence or bylaws and re-execute the deed; if the shareholders cannot attend, execute through a validly appointed notarial attorney (apoderado).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), local tax office of Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 at the AEAT office or electronically to obtain the provisional NIF (CIF) for the company. Attach the first notarial copy of the deed. Registration is immediate or within 3 days and enables bank account activation and invoicing.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the deed
Power of attorney if filing via representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, verify data vs. deed and resubmit corrected Form 036; if delay persists, request urgent processing at the AEAT counter; appeal within one month of negative resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Consejería de Economía, Hacienda y Empleo de la Comunidad de Madrid (regional treasury, Modelo 600)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days of deed execution, file Modelo 600 and pay the regional tax on documented legal acts (AJD) applicable to capital operations and the notarial act (1% of nominal capital in Madrid). The payment receipt must be presented to the Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing accrues surcharges and late-payment interest; file promptly. Self-assessment errors can be rectified via complementary Modelo 600 with the appropriate surcharge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registry Inscription and Definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first notarial copy (or green copy) of the deed, the ITP-AJD proof, and provisional NIF to the Registry. After registrar review, the company is inscribed. Immediately thereafter, apply to AEAT for the definitive NIF and issue the statutory corporate books (libros de socios, actas, registro de contratos).
required_dossiers: First/green notarial copy of the deed
Surviving power of attorney certificates (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the deed with defects (defectos), cure the defect and resubmit; a denial may be appealed to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within 30 days; after inscription, obtain definitive NIF within 5 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas de la Comunidad de Madrid (regional industrial board) in coordination with the Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo (state-level industrial policy for telecommunications equipment manufacturing).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento (municipal operating license for industrial activity under Ley 12/2012, Ley de Establecimientos) or Declaración Responsable where applicable; combined with Autorización Ambiental Unificada (AAU) under Ley 4/2014 de la Comunidad de Madrid for CNAE 2630 (manufacture of wireless CPE/5G routers).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Dirección General de Sostenibilidad y Control Ambiental, Consejería de Medio Ambiente y Ordenación del Territorio de la Comunidad de Madrid
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Tier B - Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Simplificada (simplified EIA) under Ley 21/2013, Annex II, Group 8 (electronic components manufacturing) where production capacity exceeds 500 units/day or plant area exceeds 1,000 m2; otherwise, environmental registration/comunicación ambiental under Ley 4/2014, with municipal sound and wastewater permits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewers per Real Decreto 817/2015: pH 6-9, COD ≤ 500 mg/L, TSS ≤ 250 mg/L, Cu ≤ 2 mg/L, Ni ≤ 3 mg/L; VOC emissions per Real Decreto 117/2003 with solvent management plan and exhaust limit ≤ 50 mg C/Nm3; WEEE/residue management per Ley 7/2022 and Real Decreto 110/2015 with authorized waste manager contracts; industrial noise ≤ 70 dBA per Ley 37/2003.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate per Real Decreto 2267/2004 (Reglamento de Seguridad contra Incendios en Establecimientos Industriales) issued by an authorized control body (OCA) and approved by the local fire brigade; structural and building clearance per Real Decreto 314/2006 (Código Técnico de la Edificación) with municipal building inspection; workplace safety per Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales and Real Decreto 486/1997 (workplace conditions); machinery certification per Real Decreto 1215/1997; electrical installation and accessibility clearance required for the operating license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), through its electronic headquarters (Sede electrónica de la AEAT). For an ordinary Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, AEAT administers national corporate income tax and VAT; the Spanish Tax Agency is not the competent authority for certain regional taxes in the Basque Country and Navarre.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Obtain a provisional Spanish tax identification number (NIF) for the company during formation, generally through the notary or AEAT, and obtain the definitive NIF after registration with the Commercial Registry by filing the required census declaration (Modelo 036) and supporting incorporation and registry documents. Register the SL in the tax census and declare the applicable tax activities and VAT status before commencing taxable activity. A foreign legal entity that must register for Spanish tax or VAT generally applies to AEAT for a Spanish NIF using Modelo 036 and provides evidence of its legal existence, constitutional documents, and representative's authority; document formalities may require apostille or legalization and translation. A non-EU business may be required to appoint a Spanish tax representative for VAT purposes, subject to applicable statutory exceptions. The EU VAT identification number is the Spanish NIF with the ES prefix; request inclusion in the Register of Intra-Community Operators (ROI) when conducting qualifying intra-EU transactions. Confirm current filing channels and document requirements with AEAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no US-style check-the-box election for an SL. A Spanish-resident SL is generally subject to Spanish corporate income tax on its worldwide income, subject to applicable treaty relief and statutory rules. Available elections or regimes include qualifying tax-group consolidation, the special regime for small newly created entities where eligibility conditions are met, and other opt-in regimes with specific requirements. These are not entity-classification elections. Hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions or require income inclusion in specified cross-border arrangements; they do not provide a general classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA); the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla have separate indirect-tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic turnover threshold: a person making taxable supplies in Spain must register and comply with VAT obligations from the point required by law, subject to transaction-specific rules and exemptions. The EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold applies only to specified cross-border intra-EU distance sales and electronically supplied services by qualifying suppliers, not as a general Spanish VAT registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not generally require real-time tax-authority clearance or digital stamping of every invoice. The Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) electronic VAT reporting system applies to specified businesses, including large businesses, VAT groups, and businesses registered in the monthly VAT refund regime; covered taxpayers generally report invoice-register data within four calendar days, subject to statutory exceptions. Spain's invoicing-system integrity and electronic-invoicing requirements are subject to phased implementation and current regulations; applicable obligations depend on taxpayer category and commencement dates. Public procurement invoicing has separate requirements. Verify current AEAT technical specifications and deadlines before implementation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with right to deduct under Article 21 of Spain's VAT Law, provided the statutory exporter, transport, and documentary conditions are met. Supplies of services to customers outside the EU are not automatically zero-rated; their VAT treatment depends principally on place-of-supply rules, customer status, service type, and applicable exemptions. Retain evidence establishing the transaction and, for goods, actual exit from the EU customs territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export invoice identifying the parties, goods, VAT treatment, and transaction
Electronic export declaration and export MRN, with customs confirmation of exit from the European Union
Bill of lading, air waybill, CMR, or other transport documentation evidencing dispatch to a destination outside the EU
Purchase order, contract, packing list, and proof of delivery or receipt where available
Accounting and VAT records supporting the export exemption and input-tax deduction
Bank receipt or payment evidence where available; an Inward Remittance Certificate is not a general Spanish statutory prerequisite for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain imposes no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. If export exemption is unsupported or inapplicable, AEAT may assess VAT, interest, and penalties under the General Tax Law, including penalties for inaccurate returns or tax fraud; the applicable amount depends on conduct, tax shortfall, culpability, and statutory aggravating or mitigating factors. Improperly deducted input VAT may also be disallowed or recovered. Maintain contemporaneous customs exit and transport evidence and correct returns when required.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the national central bank and euro-area monetary authority, exercising foreign-exchange and balance-of-payments statistical supervision jointly with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCI) of the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism and the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a fully convertible euro-area jurisdiction. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are generally free of exchange-control authorization under EU treaty freedoms. Dividends, interest, royalties, and trade payments to non-residents are transferable without Banco de España approval after satisfaction of corporate income-tax withholding and reporting requirements. There are no domestic foreign-exchange surrender or peg duties. Residual restrictions apply only to non-EU foreign direct investments in a limited set of sensitive sectors, financial/regulatory licensing, and EU/international sanctions screening; otherwise, no convertibility ceiling or material profit-repatriation hurdle exists. For statistical and balance-of-payments purposes, cross-border payments involving resident non-financial companies must be reported by the resident bank or by the company through the Banco de España 'Telemarcos' or equivalent electronic declaration system where transactions exceed de minimis thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Spain imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion window, and no minimum repatriation ratio for euro-area exporters. Export receipts from extra-EU sales may be held in the currency of the buyer or converted freely at market rates. However, exporters are required to ensure that export settlements are observable to the Bank of Spain for balance-of-payments statistical purposes, usually through the receiving Spanish bank; settlement must be supported by commercial invoices, customs declarations (DUA), bills of lading, and, where applicable, the applicable transaction code on the SWIFT or correspondent instruction. Non-declaration or mis-coding of export proceeds may trigger administrative penalties but does not create a repatriation obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multicurrency Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Multicurrency Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Euro Operational Account and Trade-Finance Escrow Account
Multicurrency Operational Account and Investment Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium for use as primary treasury layer; Medium only for auxiliary virtual-account concentration or FX conversion. EEA-authorized electronic money institutions (EMIs) and fintech banks passporting under the Electronic Money Directive (EMD2) and Payment Services Directive (PSD2) may legally hold euro accounts for Spanish companies and route cross-border SEPAs. However, such entities are not licensed credit institutions and cannot provide the full treasury stack required for an ISIC 2630 telecom OEM exporter: no commercial documentary letter-of-credit issuance, no Sharia or UCP trade settlement desks, no Banco de España balance-of-payments reporting as a credit institution, and often no physical Spanish branch. Non-EEA offshore EMIs without a EU/EEA authorization must not be used for corporate treasury because funds held would not be within the Spanish/EU deposit or investment protection environment; Spanish law expects the corporate to bank with an authorized bank or licensed payment institution. If used at all, an EEA-authorized EMI should be restricted to receivables concentration/API treasury operations while all trade-finance and regulated-capital transactions flow through a tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada with non-resident ownership, Spanish tier-1 banks generally require physical presence of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and at least one managing director or appointed signatory during onboarding. Where the board is wholly non-resident, the bank will typically accept a videoconference interview only under reinforced customer-due-diligence procedures, but in practice the Spanish branch also requires an in-person signing appointment for the notarized corporate opening resolution and for validation of passport/NIE documents. Higher-risk sectors such as telecom hardware OEM, being exposed to dual-use/cryptographic product classification, will trigger enhanced due diligence and a formal compliance interview; remote-only opening with power-of-attorney from a foreign jurisdiction is generally insufficient for capital escrow and documentary LC needs. The bank will also demand evidence of Spanish establishment such as a registered office, local director NIE, tax agent appointment, and, if applicable, the SL's statutory books and commercial registry certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-resident UBO chain and shareholder trust/foundation structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation and bylaws of the SL; Commercial Registry current certification; fully completed Spanish UBO register (Registro de Titularidades Reales) declaration; corporate structure chart tracing every shareholder to a natural person; official passports and NIE/TIE cards of all shareholders and directors; signed confirmation as to Source of Wealth (SOW) and Source of Funds (SOF); recent audited or management accounts; LEI certificate of the SL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 2630 wireless/5G router manufacturing raising dual-use export-control or cryptographic product flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product technical datasheets demonstrating normal commercial civil-communications function; EU Dual-Use Regulation (2021/821) classification assessment concluding either 'No Annex-I status' or the relevant Annex-I category 5A002 license exemption; corporate export-control policy; denied-party and sanctions screening results of all customers and end-users; end-user/end-use certificates for all foreign buyers; documentary evidence of any relevant telecom equipment type-approval or CE/RED certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to East-Asian component suppliers and LATAM distributors exceeding expectations for the entity's size
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed purchase orders, pro-forma invoices, and credit notes for each supply corridor; transport documents (house/sea/air waybills), customs entry records, and Intrastat/extra-EU export declarations showing physical goods movement; bank SWIFT MT101/MT103 references evidencing commercial purpose; annual business plan and inventory-flow explanation; third-party due-diligence profiles of major suppliers and distributors; trade receipts to substantiate transfer-pricing consistency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividend, interest, or royalty remittance to non-resident parent presenting tax-withholding and beneficial-ownership red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish corporate income tax certificates and model 202/200 acceptance; a formal file substantiating compliance with article 21/entity-level taxation and any applicable Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) benefits; residency certifications of the parent issued by the home tax authority; beneficial-ownership statement in Form 296/123 or tax-residency filing as required; calculation of gross and net remittance amounts; full corporate agreements resolving declared dividend or loan documentation including shareholder loans with notarised deeds, transfer-pricing documentation, and arm's length interest-rate benchmarks.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity and quasi-equity capital from the non-resident parent must enter Spain through a SWIFT MT103 or MT203 wire to the SL's domestic tier-1 account in euros or, with prior bank authorization, in a foreign currency. For subscribed share capital increases, a notary must execute the capital-increase deed, which is then registered in the Mercantile Registry; the bank further requires the tax form (model D-1A or equivalent) for payment of transfer tax/operations of legal documents where applicable. For balance-of-payments statistical classification, the remittance purpose code in SWIFT field 70 must align with 'direct investment' and not with ordinary trade or service settlement; the receiving Spanish bank will map the transaction to the Banco de España direct investment category. Example codes used in Spanish BO-P practice are the 'Form D-1A' foreign-investment declaration for entities with over 50% foreign participation (or where the non-resident investor acquires more than 10% voting rights) and the quarterly 'R.I. 1' reporting. The compliance protocol in practice is: (i) receipt of clean SWIFT funds from the parent's own bank account; (ii) parent-side financing resolutions or certificate of good standing; (iii) notarised deed and legalisation; (iv) statement of direct investment to the DGCI within one month of execution; and (v) posting of an internal capital-risk memo demonstrating that no sanctioned entity is involved. No exchange-control surcharge or prior central-bank permit applies to an SL receiving capital from an EU resident; for non-EU residents, notification only, not authorization, is mandatory except in politically defended sectors.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for outbound trade settlements are (i) SWIFT MT103 for TT/open-account wire payments to foreign suppliers and service providers; (ii) SWIFT MT700/MT710 for issuance of commercial documentary letters of credit to suppliers or confirmation of LCs received from buyers; (iii) documentary collections (DP/DA) through the bank's trade desk using SWIFT MT400-series where direct LC issuance is not required; and (iv) SEPA Credit Transfers in euro for EU suppliers. For export sales to Latin America and Asia, the entity should use totally underwritten or confirmed irrevocable LCs via its Spanish bank to mitigate buyer credit and clearing delays. All trade payments require a compliant instruction set including the invoice number, contract references, Harmonized System code, and the appropriate Spanish balance-of-payments transaction code; the bank will hold or release in accordance with dual-use, sanctions, and export-control screening. For inbound export proceeds, the Spanish bank's receiving correspondent switch will credit the SL's account upon matching SWIFT MT103 details; for amounts above the €50,000 monthly reporting threshold, the bank automatically aggregates and files the transaction with the Banco de España. Documentation of the underlying export must be retained for ten years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Cuentas Anuales including balance sheet, income statement and management report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the financial year (e.g. 30 April for calendar year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines €3,000 to €300,000+; potential administrative dissolution if not rectified

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Net turnover exceeding €8 million, total assets exceeding €4 million, or average number of employees exceeding 50

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation required; changes in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be notified to the Registro Mercantil within one month

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created entities (art. 29.3 Ley 27/2014) in the first tax period with positive tax base and the following period; 15% for certified innovative startups under Ley 28/2022 (first three tax periods with positive base, subject to limits); R&D deduction of 25% on eligible R&D costs (increased to 42% for external R&D), patent box regime 23% on qualified patent income; keeping loss carryforward unlimited (code 999 used in this file to denote perpetual), but annual offsetting capped at 50%-70% of taxable base depending on net turnover.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically via AEAT Cl@ve system (www.agenciatributaria.es) or authorized third-party software; mandatory e-filing for all corporate taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a fiscal year ending 31 December, deadline is 25 July of the subsequent year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Identification Number of the Spanish entity (or permanent establishment).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Spanish NIF assigned to the permanent establishment (NIF-ES) or the NIF of the representative for non-resident without PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National Classification of Economic Activities code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PE engaged in manufacturing of broadband routers, use CNAE 2630 (Manufacture of communication equipment).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net amount of turnover generated during the tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only turnover economically attributable to the Spanish PE in accordance with the OECD PE attribution principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable base after accounting and fiscal corrections (positive or negative).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply transfer-pricing adjustments and ensure arm’s length remuneration of the PE; carryforward losses subject to offsetting limits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic and treaty-related tax credits (R&D, double taxation relief, withholding tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach evidence of final withholding taxes paid in Spain or abroad; special documentation required for DTA relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge: 5% of amount due if filed within 3 months of deadline; 10% within 6 months; 15% within 12 months; 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. For non-filing without amount due, fine up to €1,500. For incorrect or incomplete filing, penalty up to 50% of the amount due (General Tax Law art. 27 and 27 bis).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (Non-Resident Income Tax, IRNR, Royal Decree 5/2004, art. 28.2; reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when parent holds ≥5% for ≥1 year and is resident in an EU/EEA treaty country).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the competent tax authority of its jurisdiction of residence (validity generally 1 year). The Spanish withholding agent (the SL) must submit the TRC and a Form 210/212 (non-resident tax return) through the AEAT, together with Form 02 (communication of accrued IRNR) and the treaty relief declaration. For EU shareholders, a statement of substantial ownership (≥5% held for 12 months) must be provided. If the documentation is submitted within 30 days of the distribution, the 19% withholding may be applied as a provisional rate; otherwise, a refund procedure is initiated after withholding. All filings must be made electronically.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate: 19% for any interest or royalty paid to non-residents. Under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC), exemption applies if the related company (25%+ ownership) is resident in an EU/EEA state. Under tax treaties, interest rates typically range from 0% to 10% and royalties from 0% to 15% (e.g., Spain-China treaty: interest 5%, royalties 5%; Spain-LatAm treaties often 5-10%). For substantial IP royalties (patents), treaty benefits may be restricted under the OECD Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and Local File are mandatory if the group’s consolidated net turnover ≥ EUR 45 million. Additionally, simplified transfer pricing documentation is required for any related-party transaction exceeding EUR 250,000 when the entity’s net turnover is below EUR 10 million. Country-by-Country Report filing threshold: consolidated group revenue ≥ EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not implement GCC Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but substance requirements are embedded in the general anti-abuse rule (art. 15 Ley 58/2003) and CFC rules (art. 100 Ley 27/2014). A Spanish SL must be directed, managed, and operate from Spain with adequate personnel, premises, and economic functions. If a shell company is used solely to channel funds, the AEAT may disregard the entity, reattribute income, and impose penalties (GAAR, art. 15.3) plus possible criminal liability for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional understatement of taxable income or determination of the tax assessment exceeding €120,000 in the amount evaded (art. 305 Código Penal), e.g., omitting invoicing of 5G router sales or inflating deductible expenses with fictitious invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and fine of 2 to 6 times the evaded amount; loss of subventions or tax benefits; publication of the sentence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate, approve, or fail to prevent the fraud are jointly liable for the corporate tax debt and penalties (art. 42 Ley General Tributaria); if criminal liability is established, the director may face the same imprisonment and be subject to a travel ban and prohibition of administrative management for 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Spanish SL without real business activity, used exclusively for interposing in a legal arrangement to avoid withholding taxes or to obtain treaty benefits (abuse of law, art. 15 Ley 58/2003); failure to meet the substance criteria for the manufacturing activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the transactions, recognition of Spanish-source income, and liability for unpaid withholding taxes (19% plus surcharge). Administrative penalty: from 50% to 150% of the tax amount shortfall (art. 191 Ley 58/2003). Additionally, denial of treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held civilly liable for the tax debt under the veil-lifting doctrine (jurisprudencia del Tribunal Supremo); they can be obliged to pay the unpaid corporate tax and interest personally; in severe cases, up to 10 years of disqualification from acting as director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / Lack of Beneficial Owner Disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) in the Companies Register, or failing to file the annual 'modelo de declaración de titularidad real' (BO registry); using anonymous or fiduciary vehicles to hold shares in the SL; suspicious wire transfers related to telecom equipment cross-border trade without AML filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 10,000 (or 5% of share capital for non-compliance) under Law 10/2010; in money laundering cases, criminal proceedings under art. 301 and 302 Código Penal can lead to imprisonment of 6 to 18 months and a fine up to 300% of the proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the SL are statutorily liable as 'sujetos obligados' for AML violations; they may face separate criminal imprisonment and fines, and the corporate veil can be lifted to impose personal liability for the penalties and civil damages.
